merger_description:
Dynamo Bidco, Inc., an affiliate of various funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (**Blackstone**), proposes to acquire 100% of the equity interests of DarkVision Technologies Inc. (**DarkVision**) held by Koch ES Canada Holdings, Ltd and other shareholders (the **Acquisition**).

DarkVision is a Canadian company that develops advanced ultrasound imaging technology to capture high resolution imaging data of industrial assets, including oil and gas wells and pipelines. DarkVision’s three core products globally are:

* Hades, a downhole inspection tool and ultrasound imaging system for oil and gas wells,
* Kraken, an in-line inspection tool and ultrasound platform for transmission pipelines, and
* Hydra, an ultrasonic mobile or embedded inspection device, enabled by a proprietary ASIC chip, which is in development.

In Australia, DarkVision’s activities are limited to the supply of downhole imaging services to companies in the oil and gas industry via the Hades product.

Blackstone is a US-based corporation, incorporated under the laws of Delaware, United States. Blackstone operates as an investment management firm, not as a conglomerate or holding company. Accordingly, each company in its investment portfolio is independently managed and financed and each has different investors (although the investors in different investment funds may overlap). Each Blackstone portfolio company has its own board of directors, which generally also include Blackstone representatives.

determination_table_content.details:
Dynamo Bidco, Inc., an affiliate of various funds advised and/or
managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (Blackstone), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the equity interests in DarkVision Technologies Inc. (DarkVision), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Blackstone, is a US-based corporation incorporated
under the laws of Delaware, United States. Blackstone operates as
an investment management firm, not as a conglomerate or holding
company. Accordingly, each company in its investment portfolio is
independently managed and financed, and each has different
investors (although the investors in different investment funds may
overlap). Each Blackstone portfolio company has its own board of
directors, which generally also include Blackstone representatives.
The target, DarkVision, is a Canadian company that develops
advanced ultrasound imaging technology to capture high resolution
imaging data of industrial assets, including oil and gas wells and
pipelines. In Australia, DarkVision’s activities are limited to the
supply of downhole imaging services to companies in the oil and gas
industry, via its core product, Hades. Hades is a downhole inspection
tool and ultrasound imaging system for oil and gas wells.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between Blackstone or its controlled portfolio companies and
DarkVision in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
